purpose: one baseline through the runner's existing training and validation contract, on both levels of the artifact the release will carry

artifact.source: the ten artifact files fetched from private staging by the job itself and measured in place: these are the bytes being released, not a rebuild
artifact.definition: does the station's daily maximum observed water level exceed its published NOS minor flood threshold on the target day

runner_files.note: the benchmark's own train.py, validate.py and validate.sh, copied verbatim; validate.py re-ran training and reported CONTRACT OK on both levels

dependencies: recorded in this job's container.log: pandas 2.3.3, numpy 2.5.3, xgboost 3.4.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1 (installed from the runner's declared ranges). noaa-baseline-001 did not record its versions; this rerun closes that gap for the recorded figure
scope: one baseline only. No coding agent and no harness comparison was run, and none is implied.

previous_measurement.why: measured on the superseded artifact, whose only schema difference is the label column name (`late`), copied from the Austin task. Rows and positives are identical in all six splits; the third decimal differs because xgboost's training is not bit-reproducible, so the two measurements agree to about 0.0005

calibration.question: how much of the baseline's AUC is persistence rather than prediction
calibration.method: single stock features and a plain 'yesterday exceeded' rule, no training; rank-based AUC; the eval split only

calibration_note: the persistence floor was measured with code/persistence_baseline.py against the noaa-003 eval split (staging release 392230750). The corrected artifact has identical rows and positives in every split, but a few observation values were revised between the two pulls, so those single-feature figures are carried over as measured on those bytes rather than re-measured on the released ones
